title: Medieval Europe
description: Kings, castles, crusades and plague in Europe's Middle Ages

questions.question: Which event in 476 AD is often used to mark the start of the Middle Ages?
choices: The fall of the Western Roman Empire
questions.explanation: In 476 the Germanic leader Odoacer deposed the last Western Roman emperor, Romulus Augustulus, a common starting point for the Middle Ages.

questions.question: Who was crowned Emperor of the Romans by Pope Leo III on Christmas Day, 800 AD?
questions.explanation: Charlemagne, king of the Franks, was crowned emperor in Rome in 800, reviving the idea of a western empire.

questions.question: In what year did William the Conqueror win the Battle of Hastings?
questions.explanation: William of Normandy defeated King Harold II at Hastings in 1066, beginning the Norman conquest of England.

questions.question: What document did English barons force King John to seal in 1215?
questions.explanation: Magna Carta limited the king's power and became a foundation of later ideas about the rule of law.

questions.question: What was the social system in which vassals received land in exchange for military service?
questions.explanation: Under feudalism, lords granted fiefs (land) to vassals, who owed loyalty and military service in return.

questions.question: Which pandemic killed an estimated third or more of Europe's population in the mid-1300s?
questions.explanation: The Black Death (1347-1351), an outbreak of bubonic plague, killed roughly 30-50% of Europe's people.

questions.question: Who called for the First Crusade in 1095?
questions.explanation: Pope Urban II launched the First Crusade at the Council of Clermont in 1095.

questions.question: Which young French woman led troops during the Hundred Years' War before being burned at the stake in 1431?
questions.explanation: Joan of Arc helped lift the Siege of Orléans in 1429. She was captured, tried and executed in Rouen in 1431.

questions.question: Which empire, centered on Constantinople, survived until 1453?
questions.explanation: The Byzantine (Eastern Roman) Empire lasted until the Ottomans captured Constantinople in 1453.

questions.question: Which language was used for scholarship and the Church throughout medieval Western Europe?
questions.explanation: Latin was the shared language of the Western Church, universities and learning, even as everyday speech shifted to vernacular languages.
